- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (≥ 3 consecutive +1.00), model under-forecasts; adjust upward by 3–7% for next 5 days.
- Model consistently over-forecasts in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 10–15% downward bias for first 7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2+ consecutive days below 75), model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for next 3 days.
